The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the Insurance Company under Section 30(1) of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (hereinafter referred to as 'WC Act' for short), challenging the order passed in WCA/NFC/CR/3/2010 dated 28.10.2011 by the W.C. Commissioner, Sub Division-6, Bengaluru questioning the liability fixed on the Insurance Company.
2. The undisputed facts are that the claimant was working as a driver of DCM Eicher Van bearing No.KA-40- 2824 under respondent No.2.

The claimant has sustained NC: 2023:KHC:24853 injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 17.06.2008 at about 12.30 a.m. when he was proceeding near outskirt of Pothulamadugu Village, near L&T Company, dashed against the hind portion of another vehicle.
Therefore, the claimant has filed claim petition seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the respondent No.1/claimant and perused the records.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the vehicle involved in the case is a DCM Eicher Van bearing No.KA-40-2824, which is a medium goods vehicle but the driver was holding driving license to drive light motor vehicle.
Hence, there is violation of condition of insurance policy as the driver, who drove the DCM Eicher Van was not holding driving license to drive medium goods vehicle.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the appeal.

sentences.text: 2 5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimant justified the order passed by the learned Commissioner and hence, prays to dismiss the appeal.
6. In the present case, the vehicle involved in the accident is DCM Eicher Van, which is a medium goods vehicle.
But, the driver who drove the vehicle was holding driving license to drive light motor vehicle (non-transport).
Therefore, there is a difference in class of vehicle involved in the accident and class of vehicle mentioned in the driving license.
The driver who drove the DCM Eicher Van was not having driving license to drive medium goods vehicle and caused accident, which is nothing but violation of conditions of insurance policy.
Therefore, Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation by indemnifying the owner for the aforesaid reasons.
Therefore, learned Commissioner has committed an error in fastening liability on the Insurance Company.
Accordingly, it is modified holding that the respondent NC: 2023:KHC:24853 No.2 - owner shall pay compensation to the claimant.
Accordingly, Insurance Company is exonerated.
7. Learned Commissioner has awarded compensation by correctly holding the parameters of law in assessing the compensation.

It has considered that the claimant was earning a salary of Rs.4,000/-
per month and was aged 27 years at the time of accident and accordingly, relevant factor applicable is 213.57 and considering the doctor's evidence that the claimant has suffered 24% of permanent disability has determined compensation of Rs.1,23,016/-, which is just and proper.
Hence, it does not call for interference.
Therefore, modification of quantum of compensation awarded by learned Commissioner does not arise.

8. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2023:KHC:24853 ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed.

ii. The order passed by the W.C. Commissioner in WCA/NFC/CR/3/2010 dated 28.10.2011 is hereby modified holding that the respondent No.2 - owner of the vehicle is liable to pay compensation as determined by the W.C. Commissioner to the claimant and appellant/Insurance Company is exonerated.
iii. The amount deposited by the Insurance Company shall be transmitted to the W.C. Commissioner for refunding to the appellant/Insurance Company.
iv. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Labour Court, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
NC: 2023:KHC:24853 v. Costs made easy.
vi. Ordered accordingly.
In view of the disposal of the appeal, pending application do not survive for consideration.
